subject: Intake: BYO-KMS short retention exception (ClearSky) - routing & triage
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intake: BYO-KMS short retention exception (ClearSky) - routing & triage

Folks — forwarding an ask from a prospective customer (ClearSky Health). They want to run inference on PHI-ish data but insist on: full customer-managed KMS (BYOK/HSM), and a non-standard retention window for KV/prefix cache: 7 days (instead of our default ephemeral cache policy). They characterize this as a "short retention exception" — not full long-term storage, but longer than our usual session TTLs.

Attachments: clearsky_requirements.pdf (customer requirements), proposed_keyflow.png (their suggested flow)

Key constraints from the doc:
- They will provision an HSM-backed key in their cloud account and want envelope encryption so we never hold plaintext keys.
- Audit log requirements: they need proof of key usage and request/response hashes retained for 90 days for compliance, but only the cached KV prefixes need 7 days.
- No export of KMS keys, no persistent material held by us beyond 7 days for cache.

Questions for triage:
1) Is envelope + short-lived data encryption feasible with current runtime (KV-cache invalidation + key material flow)?
2) What audit/log changes are required to meet their 90-day audit request while respecting our privacy boundaries?
3) Any legal/compliance blockers (Marcus/Evelyn) for making an exception?

Proposed immediate next step: quick sync (30m) to align on approach and list of product/infra changes and customer-facing controls (SLA/legal language).

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 08:45 AM Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@clearskyhealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Priyom — attaching a short doc with our acceptance criteria. We can sign an agreement for the shorter retention carveout if Redwood can guarantee no key export and provide audit evidence for 90 days.
> — Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: BYO-KMS short retention exception (ClearSky) - routing & triage

Thanks Priyom — quick thoughts from infra:
- Envelope encryption pattern is already supported in Dedicated and Private flows; we can accept a customer-provided KMS key (KMS-as-wrapping-key) and use envelope keys on our side. We need to ensure we do not persist the unwrapped key material.
- For the 7-day cache TTL: runtime already supports configurable KV TTLs per tenant; we would need to expose a per-account override and a purge job. That part is low friction (config + one migration).
- Audit logs: we currently store request/response traces for 30 days in the hosted plan. Extending to 90 days requires changes to retention policies and potentially storage cost/billing. We must also ensure logs do not contain raw plaintext. We can store hashes and metadata (key IDs, request IDs, timestamps).

Open technical trade-offs:
1) If we store hashes for 90 days, we need to confirm customers accept hashed payloads for forensic purposes. 
2) HSM-key usage: depending on provider, signing key operations may add latency — we should measure.

Action items I recommend for the sync:
- Product to confirm UI/contract language for per-account TTL override.
- Security to sign off on audit evidence schema (Marcus/Evelyn).
- Dev infra task: implement per-tenant retention flag + purge automation.

I can prepare a short design doc and estimate.
Karthik

> On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 09:12 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Folks — forwarding an ask from a prospective customer (ClearSky Health).

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: BYO-KMS short retention exception (ClearSky) - routing & triage

Appreciate the context. A few legal/compliance notes from my side:
- ClearSky's ask to have 90-day audit evidence is reasonable, but we need to be explicit about what that evidence contains. We cannot surface customer payloads back to them — even hashed payloads need to be validated with our privacy team.
- Any per-account exceptions should go through a documented approval path. Suggest a one-off "compliance carveout" ticket that records: scope, duration (is this permanent for that account or timeboxed?), controls required (e.g., SOC2 evidence, external audit right), and acceptance criteria.
- Pricing: extended audit retention will carry a surcharge. Let's include a short note to sales so expectations are clear.

Please loop Legal (I will ping them) and include a brief SLA sketch for Tom (what we will and won't provide).

Marcus
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

> On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 10:01 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: BYO-KMS short retention exception (ClearSky) - routing & triage

Thanks all for the quick replies. A couple clarifications from my side:
- ClearSky's compliance team needs an immutable record of key usage (key-id, operation, timestamp) and a verifiable hash of request/response for 90 days. We do not expect Redwood to store plaintext.
- The 7-day retention for cache is non-negotiable for our threat model.
- We'd sign a contract addendum and accept a surcharge for extended audit retention.

Link to our DPA addendum draft: https://acrobat.com/docusign/clearsky-dpa-draft (we will send a formal DocuSign).

Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow if helpful.

— Tom

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intake: BYO-KMS short retention exception (ClearSky) - routing & triage

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 

Summary:
- Feasible: Envelope + customer-managed KMS OK for Dedicated/Private; per-tenant cache TTL override is implementable.
- Audit evidence: we can provide key-operation logs + request/response hashes for 90 days but must confirm hashed evidence is acceptable to ClearSky. This will require a retention extension and a surcharge.
- Legal: Marcus will open a carveout ticket and loop Legal; need clarity on permanence (timeboxed vs permanent).

Immediate next steps (owners + ETA):
1) Karthik: draft design + infra estimate for per-tenant TTL override, purge automation, and audit retention change (ETA: 5 business days).
2) Marcus: open compliance carveout ticket and draft an SLA addendum; loop Legal (ETA: 3 business days).
3) Priyom: coordinate call with ClearSky (confirming hashed-evidence acceptance), capture contract ask, and collect their DocuSign when ready (ETA: schedule by EOD tomorrow).

I'll create a short Confluence page and attach the customer doc. Thanks — will follow up after Karthik's design is posted.

Priyom
